bull_bear.body: Rs 1,400 cr organic capex weighted to cables & wires + R&D; strategic renewables investment (Goldi) for supply-chain control; sustained brand investment (A&P ~2.7% of revenue) treated as long-term capital. Distribution-policy reset toward sell-out to improve channel return-on-capital. No buyback/dividend commentary on the call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Market-share erosion:** analysts repeatedly flagged Havells lagging peers in wires & cables (competitor posted high-single-digit wire / mid-single-digit cable growth; Havells ~flat) and continued AC share loss — management deflected to "sell-out reset" and long-term view.
- **Switchgear demand/geopolitics:** West Asia export disruption + trade confusion; recovery hinges on shipping normalization.
- **A&P drag persistence:** elevated Lloyd A&P for "a couple of years" caps near-term Lloyd profitability.
- **RM volatility:** copper/aluminium swings create sell-in timing distortions (dealers destock when prices fall).
- **Channel inventory** lower than normal at quarter-end for cables + ACs — could aid or distort Q2 optics.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Chairman Anil Rai Gupta was confident but notably guarded — repeatedly declined guidance ("we do not give guidance for the year"), brushed off a pointed repeat question on cables/wires share loss ("I don't need to repeat my answer"), and gave a terse "I'm always confident about Havells growth." Defends the aggressive A&P timing on first-principles (long-term brand vs short-term RM noise). CFO Rajiv Goel more forthcoming on specifics (A&P at ~2.7% of revenue, capex split, renewables margin mix). Tone: long-term-oriented, disciplined on pricing, but light on hard numbers and slightly defensive on competitive share.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The profit dip is self-inflicted and deliberate** — a >2x A&P front-load (Rs 286 cr), not a demand problem; the swing factor for the rest of FY27 is A&P normalization, not top line.
- **Switchgear is the quiet worry** — it's the highest-margin segment and lost 260 bps + 4% sales; a sustained West Asia disruption matters more to profit than the volume-flat cables optics.
- **"Sell-out" distribution reset** is the recurring explanation for soft primary volumes (Havells + Lloyd both) — aligning primary to secondary should stabilize but is masking reported growth now.
- **Renewables separation is a signaling move** — management wants investors to track a business it believes "can become very big," but repeatedly refused to size it ("too early").
- Cables capacity is up yet volumes are flat — the market is watching whether the Rs 800 cr build converts, or share continues leaking to peers.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividends paid of Rs 376 crores in Q1 FY27 and Rs 627 crores in FY26 — the dominant financing outflow in both periods.
- Debt-light balance sheet: total non-current liabilities of Rs 675 crores consist of lease liabilities Rs 174 crores, deferred tax Rs 435 crores and other Rs 65 crores, against Total equity of Rs 9,446 crores; ROCE is defined by the company as PBT TTM / Average Capital Employed TTM (Net Worth + Debt) at 23.5%.
- Cash & Cash Equivalent at end of Q1 FY27 of Rs 1,497 crores (deck notes this "also includes bank deposits"), down from Rs 2,351 crores at the beginning of the quarter and Rs 3,353 crores at the start of FY26.
- Operating Net Cash Flow was negative Rs 186 crores in Q1 FY27 (against a positive Rs 1,557 crores for FY26), driven by a Rs 636 crores change in operating assets and liabilities.
- Returns as reported by the company: ROE 18.1% (Q1 FY27) versus 17.6% (Q1 FY26), ROCE 23.5% versus 23.7%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Switchgear (highest margin):** −4% YoY, −260 bps margin; ~15% international, disrupted by West Asia (no vessels) + RM volatility causing trade destocking; normalized contribution margin 37–40%; Q2 rebound expected.
- **Cables & Wires:** volume ~flat despite added capacity; management attributes to copper/aluminium volatility + a deliberate shift from "sell-in" to "sell-out" (secondary-aligned) distribution; Rs 800 cr of FY27 capex here; capacity utilization "high" but not disclosed.
- **Lloyd (ACs):** single-digit volume, higher value; delayed summer onset + BEE-rating-driven channel destock in prior quarters; contribution margin high-single-digit, targeting double-digit; A&P-heavy (top-of-mind + premiumization).
- **ECD / Lighting:** ECD absorbed price hikes; Lighting ASP stabilized, volume growth resuming, possible price hikes ahead (electronics).
- **Renewables (new segment):** scaling rapidly; Goldi Solar = strategic module supply ("strategic insourcing"); inverters in-house; panels lower-margin than inverters; focus on residential + C&I (not utility scale).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
> Challenges Havells explicitly discussed: (a) West Asia export disruption in switchgear; (b) losing wires/cables + AC share to named-but-unnamed listed competitors; (c) copper/aluminium RM volatility. Mapped to listed names via our own files + sector knowledge.

| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| "our competitor who reported a couple of days back… reported high single-digit growth in wires and low-to-mid single-digit in cables… while we are almost flat" — losing wire/cable share | **POLYCAB · 542652** ⭐; **KEI · 517569** ⭐ (wires & cables gaining share) | HAVELLS (self, ✅ flat volumes, margin dip) | Peers out-growing Havells on a high base; Havells' sell-out reset costs near-term volume; **Med** ⭐ (peers not named but clearly implied) |
| Switchgear "impacted because there are no vessels going" — West Asia export disruption | Domestic-tilted switchgear peers less export-exposed ⭐ | HAVELLS switchgear (self, −4% / −260 bps); other West-Asia-exposed exporters | Export-shipping disruption is company/geography-specific; recovery expected Q2; **Low–Med** ⭐ |
| Lloyd AC share loss + high A&P need — "market share that we're continuously losing in ACs" | **VOLTAS · 500575** ⭐; **BLUESTARCO (Blue Star) · 500067** ⭐ (AC share gainers) | Lloyd / HAVELLS (self, ✅ AC share loss) | Competitive AC market; Lloyd needs sustained A&P to defend top-of-mind; **Med** ⭐ sector-knowledge |
| Renewables scale-up (positive) — "a lot of our products, including switchgears and cables is also positively getting affected" by renewables capex | HAVELLS (self, ✅ renewables + pull-through); solar-value-chain names | — | National renewables/grid capex pulls switchgear + cables demand; **Low–Med** (self-benefit, directional) |

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Presented as the Havells Group operating a portfolio of brands — Havells, Lloyd, Crabtree, Standard, REO and Havells Studio — with a common CARE 360 consumer service line for Havells and Lloyd.
- Demand described as resilient: "Strong Q1 revenue growth as demand was resilient despite inflationary pressures & West-Asia war related uncertainties".
- Brand-led model reinforced deliberately — "Havells stepped-up & frontloaded brand-building efforts significantly in Q1, led by media investments which would normalise for the rest of the year".
- Reported figures in this update are Havells India Standalone (P&L, segments, balance sheet, cash flow and ratios are all labelled Havells India Standalone).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Segment restructuring] Till FY26 the company reported six segments including 'Others' housing smaller emerging businesses; because some gained traction, 'Others' was broken up and now retains only Motors and Pumps.
- [Geopolitics] West Asia war-related uncertainty is named twice — as a general demand overhang and specifically as a disruption to Switchgears exports.
- [Investee] Goldi Solar is named as an investment recipient alongside associates and US subsidiaries within the Rs 610 crores FY26 investment outflow.
- [Disclosure practice] Havells commits to issuing a fresh Information Update on the day it declares financial results, including forward-looking statements on projections, estimates, expectations and outlook.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q1 profitability was hit by (1) the >2x A&P step-up (Rs 286 cr, deliberate brand reset + seasonal front-loading — "brand building is long-term, RM fluctuations are short-term") and (2) staggered RM inflation vs staggered price hikes creating timing gaps. Contribution margin held ~18.3%. Management expects normalized contribution margins from here as price hikes (avg 7–8%) catch up with RM; declined to guide reported EBITDA. Future margin upside framed as dual-play: operating leverage + mix shift to higher-growth categories.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Strong resilient top-line; A&P Rs 286 cr (>2x YoY, front-loaded) dented reported profit; contribution margin ~18.3% (stable). Switchgear −4% / −260 bps (West Asia). Lloyd AC volume single-digit, margin high-single-digit. Cables/wires volume ~flat. Renewables carved out as separate segment (scaling fast). Price hikes avg 7–8% (range 5–20%) mostly passed on. Guidance: none (policy); capex ~Rs 1,400 cr (Rs 800 cr C&W, Rs 200 cr R&D); A&P → ~2.7% of revenue; switchgear rebound Q2; Lloyd margin → double-digit; renewables margin up in H2.
- _Next Q → check: A&P normalizing (profit recovery); switchgear demand + margin rebound; cables capacity converting to volume vs continued share loss to Polycab/KEI; Lloyd contribution margin path to double-digit; renewables segment size + margin; whether "sell-out reset" volumes stabilize._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Revenue/margin:** **no annual guidance** (long-standing policy). Qualitative: "healthy outlook on margins," expects demand to improve, contribution margins to stabilize at normalized levels; declined to commit on EBITDA margin.
- **A&P:** normalizes over the full year to **~2.7% of revenue** (Rajiv Goel); Q1 front-loading unwinds; Lloyd A&P stays elevated for "the next couple of years" (premiumization).
- **Capex FY27:** **~Rs 1,400 cr** — ~Rs 800 cr cables & wires, ~Rs 200 cr new R&D centre, remainder across other businesses.
- **Switchgear:** expects a **rebound in Q2** (international + overall) as West Asia shipping normalizes; domestic stable.
- **Lloyd contribution margin:** back to **double digits "sooner than later"** (ex the seasonally weak Q2/Q3).
- **Renewables:** margin improvement expected in **H2** (as consumer-side / inverter mix rises vs low-margin panels); no size target ("too early").
- **Price hikes:** ~7–8% average already taken (range 5–20%; cables/wires highest); most passed through, small residual into Q2.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: Consumer/industrial products — no order book. Pipeline = capacity expansion (cables & wires the priority build-out), new R&D centre, and renewables adjacencies (BESS via Pixii collaboration, EV chargers, solar-cable full range). Government renewables capex is a tailwind pulling through switchgear + cables demand alongside the standalone renewables segment.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **Renewables build-out** carved out as a separate segment to signal conviction: rooftop/residential + C&I solar, inverters (in-house), **BESS** (Pixii collaboration, early), **EV chargers** — leveraging brand + distribution; "can become very big."
- **Cables & wires capacity** as a multi-year share-and-volume play (Rs 800 cr FY27 capex).
- **Lloyd premiumization** via sustained A&P to build a long-term premium brand image.
- Switchgear/cables also ride the national renewables/grid capex wave as a second-order beneficiary.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Strong resilient top-line with **calibrated 7, and cables/wires + Lloyd ACs conceding share to peers on a distribution "sell-in → sell-out" reset. Management (as always) gives **no annual guidance** but signals stabilizing contribution margins, and a strategically scaling renewables business now carved out separately.

open.item: Consumer ECD demand recovery uncertain; management wary that summer-led Q1 growth may be a one-off, not a sustained turnaround.
Rising raw material prices (copper) in late March/April flagged as a headwind that may require price increases and pressure margins.
New refrigerator plant coming up for Lloyd; refrigerators currently sourced, in-house manufacturing to improve contribution over time.
Lloyd US HVAC product still under development; meaningful traction expected next year (FY26).
Channel inventories (AC/fans/coolers) expected to normalize by end of Q3FY26; distribution channel (>50% of sales) normalized by end Q3, MT/e-com in Q4.
Q1FY26 weakness (weak summer) framed as transitory; revenue growth and margin improvement expected over coming quarters, growth in H2 with festive.
High channel and company inventory in AC/fans/coolers after weak summer; expected to take a few months (into Q2/Q3) to normalize.
Room AC industry price increase of ~5-10% needed this quarter (ex-GST) for BEE rating, copper and INR depreciation; largely offset by GST reduction at consumer level.
Lloyd/AC channel inventory (old BEE norm stock) to normalize by March 2026 as South season starts Feb, North March.
Solar/renewables real growth and Goldi supply-chain benefit to play out in H2FY26 (Q3/Q4), improving 'Others' margins.
BEE rating changes (Jan 2026) to require price hikes in AC/fans; company confident of passing on cost increases, GST reduction partly offsets.
Lloyd contribution margins to start improving in Q3FY26 with real effect in Q4FY26 as customer-support schemes withdrawn and under-absorption eases.
Elevated working capital (cables and Lloyd) expected to normalize by Q4FY26; other income to stay relatively low in H2 given planned capex.
BEE norm change (Jan 2026) not seen as a challenge given own factories and manageable inventory levels.
Company (ex-Lloyd) to return to normalized margin levels in FY26 as manpower investments yield efficiencies and growth.
